For instance, many Indigenous students received access to basic literacy and numeracy skills, as well as vocational training in areas such as agriculture, crafts, and domestic work. While these experiences were undoubtedly shaped by the power dynamics of the time, they also demonstrate the resilience and adaptability of Indigenous communities in the face of imposed assimilation.

Another critical aspect to consider is the role of the residential schools system in promoting educational opportunities for Indigenous students. While the system was undoubtedly flawed and exploitative, it did provide a limited form of access to education for many Indigenous children who would otherwise have had little or no access to formal schooling. Furthermore, some accounts suggest that certain residential schools did offer advanced education and vocational training, including programs in medicine, law, and the arts.

It is essential to emphasize that these potential positive impacts on Indigenous communities should not be used to justify or downplay the gross injustices and human rights abuses committed within the residential schools system. **Safer Alternatives (10 minutes)**
